facts: The paper is titled 'Causal inference in staggered adoption panels: The correct comparison set depends on your intervention' and is authored by Ian Lundberg and Yaling Xu.
The paper was posted to arXiv on October 22, 2026 (arXiv:2610.31537).
Staggered adoption panels involve many units observed over many periods where some units adopt an irreversible treatment at different points while others remain untreated.
Popular causal methods used in this setting include difference in difference, fixed effects, matching, and synthetic control.
Existing methods aim to evaluate what outcomes treated units would realize if they had remained untreated, but this question conceals two distinct causal queries.
The first causal question evaluates outcomes under a momentary intervention that prevents treatment only at the factual adoption time.
The second causal question evaluates outcomes under a longitudinal ban that prevents treatment across all periods up to outcome measurement.

Both questions can be answered under conditionally ignorable treatment adoption or parallel trends, but common methods fail for the second question because it necessitates a time-varying comparison set with time-varying weights.
